newsitem.title: CROATIA: Blast damages monastery in divided Bosnian town.
newsitem.headline: Blast damages monastery in divided Bosnian town.

text.p: An explosive device damaged a Franciscan monastery in central Mostar, a Bosnian town where the European Union is struggling to unite rival Croat and Moslem communities.
"Some unnamed people threw an explosive substance over the wall of the monastery last night," Howard Fox, spokesman for the West European police in Mostar, told Reuters on Tuesday.
The monastery lies on the Boulevard, one of the main city streets which separated Croats and Moslems during the 10-month war they fought for control of the city in 1993.
Fox said the explosion slightly damaged the monastery wall. Croatian state news agency HINA said the explosion also shattered windows, but injured no one.

Friar Ivan Sevo told HINA he was surprised the monstery was the target. "It is well known that this very monastery helped all Mostar residents during the war, regardless of faith or nationality," he said.

The two rival ethnic groups held their first democratic elections in June, supervised and monitored by the European Union, and elected a single city administration. But it took another two months to appoint a Croat mayor and a Moslem deputy.
